assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, active GLP-1(7-36) amide) led to therapies that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care and now show cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity of mechanism and lasting impact are all high.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, intestinal growth and DPP-4 axis, translational framing) and Mojsov (identification of the biologically active peptide) form a plausible three-person set. Habener and Knudsen (industrial development of liraglutide/semaglutide) are also argued for; Habener is not on the supplied list, so the allocation is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of independent confirmation, multiple approved drugs, large outcome trials; recognition is clearly timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for identifying active GLP-1 is disputed between academic groups; Habener is absent from the supplied credited names.
Whether a drug-development contributor (Knudsen) should displace a basic scientist is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, establishing a new therapeutic modality in cancer. High originality and substantial clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early costimulated CAR design) and June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in leukemia) are central; Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials. Other contributors (Eshhar, Kuwana, Finney, Zhao) are not on the supplied list; I rely on my own recall of this history and have not verified it.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent multi-center confirmation; timing is mature, though long-term safety, secondary malignancy and solid-tumor limits remain.
uncertainties: Attribution is crowded and partly outside the supplied names.
Durability of benefit and breadth beyond hematologic cancers are still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signaling logic from the ER to the nucleus (Ire1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, ATF6, PERK) and underlies understanding of proteostasis in secretory cells, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. Conceptually clean and original, with strong RNA-processing aspects.
assessment.attribution: Walter (Ire1 and the pathway, unconventional splicing mechanism) and Mori (HAC1 and UPR transcriptional response) provide a natural two-person configuration. Ron and others contributed to the integrated stress response branch but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is stable and extensively confirmed over 30 years; therapeutic translation (e.g., ISRIB, IRE1 inhibitors) is early, but basic maturity is high.
uncertainties: Clinical impact is mostly indirect so far.
Contributions from the PERK/ISR branch may need separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP and activation of STING defines a central innate immune pathway relevant to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunity. Clear, original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP) and Barber (STING identification) are the decisive contributors; the other credited names (Sun, Wu, Ishikawa) are important co-discoverers or trainees whose roles are less distinct in prize terms. Vance, Cai and others are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Basic pathway strongly confirmed; therapeutic agonists/antagonists are still in clinical development, so the clinical consequences are not yet established.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should be tied to a clinical translation not yet realized.
Relative weighting of Chen versus Barber and the junior co-discoverers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide modulation of SMN2 exon 7 splicing (nusinersen) turned mechanistic understanding of splicing into the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, with dramatic clinical effect and a template for RNA-targeted medicine.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing regulatory mechanism and ASO design for exon inclusion) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are the two principal contributors; the pairing is coherent. Others (Singh, Hua, Adrian) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with years of real-world follow-up; maturity strong, with newer SMA modalities adding context.
uncertainties: Prior antisense chemistry work by others is not credited.
I have a field-adjacent interest in RNA processing; I weight this on the evidence rather than my area.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR identification and the mTOR pathway established a master regulator linking nutrients, growth factors and cell growth, with consequences for cancer, metabolism, aging and immunosuppression. Very high impact and broad reach.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR in yeast and defined its role in growth control, and Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin underpinned the target identification. Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work is important but his standing is complicated by reported institutional issues; I note this as uncertain and not independently verified. Heitman and Brown are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Pathway extensively confirmed; clinical (rapalogs, transplant) consequences are mature, though cancer therapy outcomes are mixed.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and others is contested.
Relationship of rapamycin chemistry to the signaling discovery needs weighing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided a general method for causal, millisecond-precision control of defined cell types and has transformed neuroscience, with emerging therapeutic use (vision restoration). Highly original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and the demonstration in neurons and the toolkit (Deisseroth, Boyden) are both decisive; with a maximum of three, I choose Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann, leaving Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck unrecognized, which is a real fairness problem.
assessment.maturity: Method confirmed by thousands of studies; clinical translation is still very early.
uncertainties: Six credited names exceed the three-person limit.
Whether a tool/method is prioritized over discoveries of biological mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis, and that its blockade works in patients, launched biologic therapy for chronic inflammatory disease across several indications.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini led the translational discovery chain from cytokine cascade evidence to the clinical trials of anti-TNF; the pairing is coherent. Contributions of Cerami, Vilcek, Kollias and others to TNF biology are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of clinical use and confirmation; recognition is mature, perhaps late, though already honored by Lasker/Breakthrough-type awards (from my own recollection).
uncertainties: Credit for the TNF molecule itself versus the therapeutic concept may require broader attribution.
Biosimilar-era maturity may reduce perceived novelty.
